subject: Lock and scale: Eval handoff + tranche plan for Aurora Health POC
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@aurorahealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurora Health Procurement <procurement@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity timeline + MAP for Aurora Health POC

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's latency/cost profile. Before we lock internal approval, procurement needs a clear mutual action plan (MAP) and a realistic timeline for Dedicated vs Private deployment lead times and recommended GPU pool sizing for our evaluation (POC) and then production.

Top asks from our side:
- A draft MAP with milestones, deliverables, and acceptance criteria tied to the POC (2–4 week eval window).
- Lead times: how long to reserve Dedicated capacity in us-west vs timeline for an on-prem Private package (approx weeks).
- A recommended GPU tranche plan (eval tranche -> pilot -> prod) with SKU equivalencies and cost/commit estimates.
- Any compliance prerequisites (SOC2 evidence, network checklist) that will block procurement.

We'd like to get to a signed PO or reservation commitment within 5 business days after the POC if the results meet acceptance criteria — please call out gating items. I've attached a one-page requirements sheet for context.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
VP Engineering, Aurora Health

Attachments: aurora_requirements_onepager.pdf (pdf)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity timeline + MAP for Aurora Health POC

Hi Maya — great to hear and appreciate the clarity. I've sketched a compact MAP and tranche approach that maps to your asks; see the attached drafts (Aurora_MAP_draft_20261011.xlsx, gpu-sizing-estimate.csv). High-level:

- Eval tranche (2 weeks): 4 x A100-80GB equiv (or 8 x A10/40GB equiv) as a short, latency-focused pool for realistic workload testing.
- Pilot tranche (4–8 weeks): scale to 12 x A100-80GB equiv to validate throughput, autoscaling, and caching strategies.
- Prod reservation (committed): 24+ vGPU-equivalent units depending on concurrency — we recommend reserving in tranches to reduce lead-time risk.

Lead times (ballpark):
- Redwood Dedicated (hosted reserved capacity): provisioning in-region typically 8–12 weeks from signed commitment for tranche >=16 GPUs; small eval tranches can often be accommodated in 2–4 weeks via burst/beta capacity.
- Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem): packaging, network, and KMS setup typically 12–16 weeks, subject to data center approvals and hardware procurement windows.

Acceptance criteria (for POC):
- Throughput: 95th pct latency under target (TBD) across the sample prompt set.
- Cost: token-unit cost within agreed threshold in MAP.
- Reliability: sustained 99.9% successful token stream for 24h of stress testing.

I'll loop in Ben and Marissa to finalize commercial milestones and Lauren to confirm SOC2 artifacts and the network checklist. Do you have a procurement contact and preferred PO template? If you can share availability, we can schedule a 30-min alignment tomorrow.

I've attached the draft MAP and a quick GPU sizing CSV — please treat as working drafts.

– Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Aurora_MAP_draft_20261011.xlsx (xlsx), gpu-sizing-estimate.csv (csv)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Aurora MAP — tranche plan and owner list (please review)

Team — looping you in with Maya's asks and the draft MAP I shared. Quick internal plan and asks:

1) Commercial milestone (Ben): finalize list price vs commit tiers, and prepare a concise one-pager for procurement (PO language + SOW summary). Target: send to Maya by EOD 10/12.
2) Solutions & eval scope (Marissa): validate the eval tranche sizing (4x A100 equiv) will cover the sample workload Maya sent. If not, propose a concrete alternate (CPU/K80 no). Provide a minimal runbook for the 2-week eval (ingest dataset, prompts, monitoring hooks).
3) Security & compliance (Lauren): confirm which SOC2 artifacts and network attestations are safe to share now; call out any redlines that require legal or CISO review.
4) Ops lead (Ben/Marissa): who will own the initial deployment launches (day 0–7) and the acceptance test window? Recommend Ben owns commercial + go-live, Marissa owns technical acceptance.

Draft timing (we need crisp dates in the MAP):
- 10/13: Agree MAP and eval dates (Maya to confirm)
- 10/16–10/30: Eval tranche (2 weeks + buffer)
- 11/01–11/21: Pilot tranche (3 weeks validation + load testing)
- 11/22+: Prod reservation finalization and procurement (commits/pricing) — provisioning window 8–12 weeks if Dedicated; 12–16 if Private.

Risks to call out in the MAP: hardware SKU shortages (Q4 risk), SOC2 evidence lag, and networking approvals (customer firewall/VPC peering).

Please reply with the short confirmations below so I can produce a single MAP file for Maya:
- Ben: confirm commercial one-pager & who owns PO template
- Marissa: confirm eval sizing/runbook
- Lauren: list of shareable compliance artifacts

Thanks — Vivek
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@aurorahealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lock and scale: Eval handoff + tranche plan for Aurora Health POC

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear asks. Per Vivek's draft, we've finalized a compact MAP and a tranche-first procurement path. Key bullets below, and the attached PDF contains the MAP milestones and acceptance criteria. Drive link with the artifacts is here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Aurora-POC-MAP

Summary (finalized):
- Eval tranche (10/16–10/30): 4 x A100-80GB equiv; Redwood hosted — chargeable as short-term evaluation credits. Deliverables: runbook, telemetry dashboard, daily check-ins.
- Pilot tranche (11/01–11/21): 12 x A100-80GB equiv to validate autoscaling and batch economics.
- Prod reservation (committed): recommended starting commit 24 GPU-equivalent units; split into 8/8/8 tranches to reduce provisioning lead time and cost shock.

Lead-time expectations:
- Dedicated (hosted reserved capacity): 8–12 weeks to full tranche provision for >16-unit commits in us-west. We can often accommodate an eval tranche within 2–4 weeks using existing capacity pools; we'll guarantee burst capacity for the POC window.
- Private (VPC or on-prem package): 12–16 weeks. This includes on-site network testing, customer KMS integration, and optional HSM timeline.

Commercial & procurement steps:
1) We will send a 1-page commercial summary + SOW (today).
2) Aurora sends PO or DocuSign approval on the agreed commit for prod tranche(s).
3) We begin provisioning immediately for eval/pilot; prod tranche provisioning timeline begins on signed commit.

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- Latency: P99 under agreed threshold for the sample prompt set.
- Functional: model outputs must pass the Aurora QA prompt set with >=95% pass rate on defined metrics.
- Operational: tracing/alerts configured and token cost within budget.

Blocked items: SOC2 audit report (we can provide SOC2 Type II summary and select evidence — Lauren is cc'd for details), and your procurement PO template.

Next steps:
- Maya: please confirm 10/16 start for the eval tranche and share the procurement contact/PO template.
- If confirmed by 10/13 EOD, we will: finalize the MAP doc, issue the eval credits, and schedule the 30-min kickoff for 10/15.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-terms-v2.pdf (pdf), Aurora_MAP_final_20261013.pdf (pdf)
